summary: The candidate now derives all 57 non-source frozen/target path tokens and all 33 closed post-reveal comparison/adjudication identifiers in the checked inventory, with no missing manifest-frozen or unit target paths. The blindness boundary is still bypassable because source_only_payload_failures checks string values but not JSON object member names. A forbidden post-reveal identifier can therefore be serialized as a key by both canonical prompt modes. Candidate-3 unit-scoped evidence remains the controlling evidence and was not contradicted by this targeted review.

findings.title: Forbidden post-reveal identifiers in JSON object keys bypass source-only preflight
findings.contract: Both canonical prompt modes must reject every member of the derived source-only forbidden inventory before any prompt write, regardless of whether the token occurs as a JSON value or object member name.

evidence.detail: The dict branch recurses into each child value and uses the key only to build the diagnostic location. It never compares the key itself with forbidden_identifiers, while identifier matching exists only in the string-value branch.
Completeness and blind modes both rely on validate_source_only_json before main writes expected bytes, so the shared key omission reaches both canonical prompt modes.
The inventory control injects identifiers only inside a string value and does not exercise forbidden identifiers as object keys or exhaust both CLI modes before write.

findings.impact: A packet or accepted completeness-review JSON can contain a closed post-reveal field name such as rootCauseId, authorityOverride, or verificationEvidenceRefs as an object key and the canonical prompt builder will not report that inventory member. Because the prompt builder does not schema-validate these payloads itself, it can emit the leaked identifier before a separate validator rejects the object shape.
minimalFix: When traversing a dict, check each string key against forbidden_identifiers before recursing into its value, exempting only the explicitly justified shared source identifiers.
Add inventory-driven controls that iterate every forbidden identifier as a JSON key and every forbidden path/identifier as a string through completeness and blind canonical CLI modes.
For each rejected CLI case, assert that a previously absent output remains absent and a pre-existing sentinel output remains byte-identical.
